title: Digging: a passage his own size, or the free-hand bite
question: Same scene, same 105 bites, same spoil setting - only the cut SHAPE differs. One is the round bite at the cursor that ships today; the other cuts a rectangle sized to the gnome, in whichever of four directions you point, and draws the box before it cuts. Which reads better as a tunnel a gnome dug? Look at the roof, the floor, and the far end.
context_md: 105 bites in both arms, same dig_yield. Dusted 3410 (free) vs 3548 (bore). He ends at y=305 in one and y=298 in the other: the free bite drifts DOWN 7 cells over the run, riding its own spoil, while the bore keeps a floor level with his feet by construction. zoom=3, cropped on the gnome (uncropped, both are a dark smear at this world size).

items.label: FREE - round bite at the cursor (current)
BORE - a passage his size, four directions (new default)
